vendors.name: Microsoft Clipchamp

Premium therefore has no monthly price recorded, rather than borrowing the Microsoft 365 rate, which is a different product. Also re-confirmed and notable: the free tier exports 1080p with NO watermark, and watermark-free export, AI editing tools and recording are present on both tiers — the real split is resolution (1080p vs 4K) and premium stock plus brand kit. Microsoft 365 prices are carried only as corroboration for the route to premium features.

plans.name: Free

Premium unlocks up to 4K UHD export, premium stock assets and the brand kit. Buyers should note they are buying an Office suite, not just a video editor.

vendors.name: Adobe Premiere Elements
vendors.provenance: adobe.com/products/premiere-elements.html re-fetched on 2026-09-10. Every figure confirmed: US$99.99 for Premiere Elements 2026, US$149.99 for the Photoshop Elements bundle, US$79.99 upgrade for Premiere Elements alone, US$119.99 bundle upgrade, US$79.99 for students and teachers, and a 'free, full-featured 7-day trial'. An earlier version of this record's central correction also held on re-fetch and is the most important thing on this record: Adobe frames this as 'a one-time purchase with no additional fees' but the same page calls it a '3-year term license' and states 'the license is non-renewing — it expires 3 years after redemption'. It is therefore recorded as a term licence, not a perpetual one, and no monthly price is recorded throughout since no monthly billing is offered. This is Premiere ELEMENTS, a distinct consumer product, not Premiere Pro.

plans.name: Premiere Elements 2026
plans.notes: One-time payment of US$99.99 with no monthly option, so no monthly price is recorded. The catch a buyer will be caught by: this is NOT a perpetual licence despite the one-time framing — Adobe describes a '3-year term license' and states it is 'non-renewing — it expires 3 years after redemption'. Averaged over the term that is about $2.78 a month, but access stops at the end of year three and you buy again.

plans.name: Premiere Elements 2026 + Photoshop Elements 2026 bundle
plans.notes: One-time payment of US$149.99 for both applications, saving $50 against buying them separately at $99.99 each. Same non-renewing 3-year term licence, so no monthly price is recorded.

plans.name: Upgrade pricing
plans.notes: One-time US$79.99 to upgrade Premiere Elements alone, or US$119.99 for the bundle upgrade. Students and teachers are quoted US$79.99. Available to existing Elements owners only, and the upgraded licence carries the same non-renewing 3-year term.

vendors.name: LumaFusion (LumaTouch)
vendors.provenance: luma-touch.com/purchase was re-fetched and again publishes no prices — it states only that 'LumaFusion is a 1-time purchase and can be purchased in any of the app stores' (Apple App Store, Google Play, Chrome Web Store, Samsung Galaxy Store) — so figures come from the US Apple App Store listing, re-fetched 2026-09-10. Prices confirmed: app $29.99; Speed Ramping & Keyframing, Multicam Studio, FCPXML Export and CoreMelt PaintX at $19.99 each; Creator Pass at $9.99/month or $69.99/year. Two substantive corrections applied on this read. First, an earlier version of this record claimed Creator Pass bundles all the $19.99 packs; the listing states it unlocks Speed Ramping, Multicam Studio and FCPXML Export plus Storyblocks content — the CoreMelt PaintX plug-in is not listed as covered. Second, an earlier version of this record's buying advice was arithmetically false: it said three or more packs cost more than a year of Creator Pass, when 3 x $19.99 = $59.97 is LESS than $69.99. That guidance has been inverted to match the arithmetic. Creator Pass is the only plan here with a real month-to-month rate; everything else is one-time and has no monthly price recorded.

plans.name: LumaFusion app (one-time)
plans.notes: One-time purchase of $29.99 on the US App Store — not a subscription, so no monthly price is recorded. Buys the full multi-track editor. Sold per app-store platform (Apple App Store, Google Play, Chrome Web Store, Samsung Galaxy Store), so buying on iPad does not license the Android or ChromeOS build; a cross-platform editor pays more than once.

plans.name: Creator Pass (subscription)
plans.notes: $9.99 per month month-to-month — a genuine monthly rate, which is why it is the only monthly price recorded for this vendor — or $69.99 per year as an annual in-app purchase. Optional, and additive on top of the $29.99 app: it does not replace the app purchase, which is the thing buyers miss. It unlocks Speed Ramping & Keyframing, Multicam Studio and FCPXML Export (three of the four paid packs, NOT the CoreMelt PaintX plug-in) and adds Storyblocks content — over a million royalty-free media assets. Features stay unlocked only while the subscription is active.

plans.name: Individual feature packs (one-time)
plans.notes: Each enhanced feature is a $19.99 one-time in-app purchase, so no monthly price is recorded. The App Store listing shows Multicam Studio $19.99, Speed Ramping & Keyframing $19.99, FCPXML Export $19.99 and the CoreMelt PaintX plug-in $19.99. Do the arithmetic before subscribing: buying outright all three packs that Creator Pass covers costs $59.97 once, which is less than a single $69.99 year of the Pass and keeps them permanently. Creator Pass only wins if you want the bundled Storyblocks library, or prefer $9.99 for a month or two of occasional access.
